problem: Time-Sensitive QA requires using specific temporal contexts and time-evolving facts, but large language models have limited sensitivity to temporal information and inadequate temporal reasoning capabilities.
method: Temporal Information-Aware Embedding plus Granular Contrastive Reinforcement Learning to enhance temporal awareness and reasoning in LLMs for time-sensitive QA.
key_assumptions: Temporal information within questions and time-evolving facts can be embedded and exploited
Reinforcement learning with granular contrastive signals improves temporal reasoning
main_contribution: A framework enhancing temporal awareness and reasoning in LLMs via Temporal Information-Aware Embedding and Granular Contrastive Reinforcement Learning, evaluated on four TSQA datasets.
datasets: Four TSQA datasets (names not stated in abstract)
benchmarks: Four TSQA datasets (names not stated in abstract)
metrics: not stated in abstract (TSQA task performance implied)
results: The framework significantly outperforms existing LLMs on TSQA across four datasets.
limitations: Addresses reader/model temporal reasoning rather than retrieval ranking over document versions

relation_to_idea.conceptual_difference: Improves the reader/model's temporal reasoning via embeddings and reinforcement learning instead of adjusting retrieval rank; no notion of document versions, supersession, or validity intervals.
relation_to_idea.basis: Abstract shows a model-side temporal-reasoning intervention evaluated on TSQA datasets; no retrieval component, versioned corpus, or temporal ranking term.
